Optimization: Higher resolutions gain detail, however have a higher fill-rate performance cost. Regardless of the setting, shadow res reduces further into the distance. If this setting is insufficient, check the following:
Scene Light Count If there are more shadowing lights than memory can bear, all shadows will be downres'ed until all fit.
Light Angle A shadow map must cover the entirety of the lit area, so wide angles on spot lights, or point lights that affect a great area will see their effective shadow resolution decrease as it's spread thinner over a greater area.
Note: Point lights actually generate 6 shadow maps, one for each cardinal axis direction/face of a cube, so they are 6x the cost of a spot light in terms of shadow cost.

This is the number of additional detail levels that should be added to the terrain when detail displacement is enabled (for example, if the value is 3, then a 32 x 32 quad tile can go to 64 x 64, then 128 x 128, and finally to 256 x 256 ).

If checked, detail displacement will be applied to the heightfield; otherwise the materials will be layered flatly onto the terrain.

This enables detail displacement on all layers (it cannot be enabled individiually).  Detail displacement will adjust the heightfield further to add the layers' heights onto the terrain.  Note that there is no collision on detail displacement, so it will be possible to see clipping with models and actors.  All layers must have a working detail offset in order for this feature to work properly.

The string value that will be imported into Houdini.  It will be accessible as a detail attribute using the tag name.

This tag can be used to access data in Houdini.  If the data associated with this element is geometry, that geometry will be grouped by this tag for easy access in Houdini.  The scalar value for this tag will be added as a detail attribute as well, so things like floating point values can also be accessed.  Tags can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores.
